scenes.voice: One client can take your API down. Rate limiting stops that. Here are two ways to do it.
Fixed window counts requests per slot, like 100 a minute. It's simple, but bursts at a window edge can double up.
Token bucket refills tokens at a steady rate. Each request spends one. Short bursts are fine, long floods aren't.
When you reject, return 429 and a Retry-After header, so well-behaved clients know when to come back.
Limit per user or API key, not just per IP. Save this for the next time you ship a public endpoint.
If this helped, follow, like, share, and subscribe.
